reason: The cited evidence (E1, E3) confirms TiB2 formation, microstructural refinement, and improved wear/corrosion resistance at x=1, but does not demonstrate that TiB2 mechanically anchors or reinforces the passive film to reduce spallation under combined tribo-corrosion; this mechanistic link is hypothesized without direct support.
premises: Boron addition to AlCoCrFeNiMoTi forms TiB2 particles in situ during laser cladding
TiB2 particles refine the microstructure and mechanically reinforce the passive film
Reinforced passive film is less prone to spallation under wear, maintaining protective continuity
Optimal boron content (~1 at.%) maximizes wear and corrosion resistance
Excessive boron leads to oversized TiB2 particles that degrade performance
